quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Bad braking technique:

options.text: Usually causes no problems.
Causes many motorcycle crashes.
Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Bad braking technique causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking is important for safe riding.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on during the day and night whenever it is legal and safe. Your high beam headlight helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: The front brake should:

options.text: Only be used in emergencies.
Be used together with the rear brake.
Never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: At intersections
On the highway
On any road

questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen at intersections. The biggest danger is oncoming cars turning left in front of motorcycles.

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Must allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: Eye and face protection is required by law. A good face shield protects your face during a crash. It must allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: There is usually an oily strip in the center of a traffic lane. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of the lane. The oil is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride on either side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: To help others see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight.
Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on is the best way to help other drivers see you. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips barely reach the handlebars when seated.
The seat is one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet touch the ground comfortably when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet touch the ground comfortably when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet comfortably touch the ground while you are seated. Make sure a motorcycle fits before you ride it.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow.
Be slightly bent at the elbow.
Be fully extended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent at the elbow.
questions.explanation: Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm tiredness and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
Both brakes are equally powerful.

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When is there less traction available for braking?

options.text: When a motorcycle is leaning.
When a motorcycle is straight up and down.
When a motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as during a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do with their mirrors?

options.text: Check them frequently.
Only the lead rider should check them.
Do not check them often because they are distracting.

questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often. This helps you see the riders behind you and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding?

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Uncomfortable clothing.

questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even during the day. Reflective materials on your clothing also help.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead.
Crossroad ahead.
Divided roadway ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign tells you that the road is divided ahead.

questions.question: How should you position your body on a motorcycle?

options.text: Hold yourself up with your arms.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Good riding posture means using your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when you hold the handgrips.

questions.question: Where do most motorcycle and car accidents happen?

options.text: At intersections.
On the open road.
In parking lots.

questions.explanation: Most collisions between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.

questions.question: If a rider wears a helmet during a crash, are they more likely to survive?

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed.
The drinker's height.
The temperature outside.

questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake supply?

options.text: About one-quarter.
About one-half.
About three-quarters.

questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: They have definitely seen you.
It doesn't always mean they've actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doesn't always mean they've actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know if a driver has seen you. A driver can look directly at you and still fail to notice you.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Be parked at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
Be parked without any wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be parked at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle should be parked at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn only your head.
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Turn only your head to look through a turn. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it can cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to help stabilize the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it can cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to slow down the bike during the U-turn.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Keep a safe following distance from each other.
Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about the distance between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe following distance from each other.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This lets riders stay close together while keeping safe following distances between them.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that turns on when the ignition is on and the bike is in neutral.
